sources.title: SQLite FTS5 manual
sources.version_or_context: Living manual, accessed 2026-10-12; actual notebook runtime unknown
sources.finding_and_applicability: Build-dependent. Unicode61 uses Unicode 6.1 and documented diacritic exceptions. Ordinary contentless CRUD differs from 3.43.0+ contentless-delete; legacy delete needs original values. External content is caller-synchronized. REBUILD reads internal or external content, unavailable without content. External comparison needs rank=1. Trigram MATCH misses substrings under three Unicode characters; LIKE/GLOB optimization is conditional. Tokens truncate at 32768 bytes. Deleted-term retention and secure-delete have distinct cost/version conditions.

sources.title: SQLite WAL
sources.finding_and_applicability: Readers can overlap a writer; one writer remains. Long readers can inhibit checkpoints. Local shared-memory coordination and cross-file atomicity limitations constrain sidecars/rebuilds; actual store is unspecified.

sources.title: SQLite ATTACH
sources.finding_and_applicability: Cross-file crash atomicity depends on non-memory main and non-WAL journal. Separate persistence domains justify canonical durable change capture and post-index-commit acknowledgement.

sources.title: SQLite nested update trigger report
sources.locator: corrected reproducer post 3 and maintainer response post 4
sources.finding_and_applicability: Initial reproduction lacked insert synchronization. Corrected example combines same-table nested AFTER UPDATE with FTS synchronization and token-superset change. Maintainer explains ordering and suggests folding the mutation into the original write. A report/workaround, not independently executed or a current universal defect.

sources.title: Tantivy IndexWriter
sources.finding_and_applicability: Commit blocks/persists/publishes; delete affects earlier operations and needs commit. Adds may block. Opstamps and commit payloads support app progress alignment; do not make source and index atomic.

sources.title: Tantivy IndexReader
sources.finding_and_applicability: Default reload can lag by tens of milliseconds; use one searcher snapshot per query. Index commit and query visibility are separate.
